title: store.Save() drops unknown JSONL fields on round-trip (design, notes) against full-beads files
description:
internal/store/store.go Save()/SaveToFile() re-encode every issue from types.Issue, so any JSON key absent from that struct is silently destroyed on the next write. Load()/loadFromFile() discards them at unmarshal time.

bd-lite's types.Issue knows 14 keys. Upstream beads writes more (design, acceptance_criteria, notes, estimated_minutes, external_ref, source_repo, content_hash, created_by).

Blast radius measured against ~/projects/beads-tui/.beads/issues.jsonl (164 issues, tracked by real beads until Feb 2026, now on bd-lite via PATH):
  design      6 issues  (tui-qxy.1/.2/.4/.5/.7, tui-tjf -- tui-tjf holds a full theme-system architecture doc)
  notes       5 issues  (tui-1oj holds a multi-paragraph root-cause writeup)
  created_by  1 issue   (tui-6f1)

Any single bd create/update/close/comment/dep-add in that repo rewrites all 164 lines and drops all of the above. Recoverable from git (issues.jsonl is tracked) but entirely silent.

This blocks filing the beads-tui sister ticket for created_by, since doing so with the bd on PATH would trigger the loss.

Fix options:
  a) widen types.Issue with every upstream field -- brittle, upstream keeps adding
  b) preserve unknowns generically: Extra map[string]json.RawMessage plus custom MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON -- robust, keeps bd-lite a lossless citizen of the beads wire format
  c) document bd-lite as lossy against full-beads files and refuse to write when unknown keys are present
close_reason: types.Issue now round-trips unknown JSONL keys via Extra map; marshalNoEscape prevents HTML re-escaping of design/notes

title: Record created_by on issue create via new internal/actor; unify cmd/comment.go author
description:
Add CreatedBy string `json:"created_by,omitempty"` to types.Issue, after Assignee. Wire-compatible with upstream beads (beads/internal/types/types.go:40).

New package internal/actor with Name(): $BD_ACTOR -> git config user.name -> $USER -> "" (field omitted). gitUserName is a package-level var func so tests stub it without a temp git repo. Trimmed from upstream's chain: no --actor flag, no $BEADS_ACTOR, no literal "unknown" sentinel.

Call Name() lazily at the two write sites. Do NOT hoist into rootCmd.PersistentPreRunE, which would fork a git subprocess on every bd list/show/ready.

cmd/create.go: set CreatedBy: actor.Name().
cmd/comment.go: drop os/user import, pass actor.Name() to st.AddComment. Behavior change: new comments record the git display name where they used to record the OS username. Existing comments render unchanged.
Dependency.CreatedBy (types.go:93) stays dead; nothing displays it.
bd update / bd close do not touch created_by.

Display: suffix the existing Created line in output.go PrintIssue, omitting the suffix when absent so legacy issues render byte-identically.
  Created:  2026-07-09 12:07 by Andy Nutter-Upham
  Created:  2026-06-30 17:45

Tests: internal/actor/actor_test.go covers the four resolution branches with t.Setenv + stubbed gitUserName. output_test.go asserts the by-suffix appears with CreatedBy set and the line is unchanged without it.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-whodunnit-design.md
close_reason: created_by stamped on create via internal/actor; comment author unified to the same helper; bd show suffixes the Created line and is unchanged when the field is absent

title: Show age column in bd list/ready; extend output.Age() past days and split out formatAge
description:
internal/output/output.go:251 defines Age() and nothing calls it. Wire it into PrintIssueList as a right-aligned 4-wide column between type and title:

  fmt.Printf("%s %s  P%d  %-12s %4s  %s\n", status, issue.ID, issue.Priority, issue.IssueType, Age(issue.CreatedAt), issue.Title)

  [ ] bd-lite-x1y  P2  feature        2h  Record whodunnit on beads
  [>] bd-lite-c3d  P1  bug           12d  Fix dep tree direction
  [ ] bd-lite-z8w  P4  chore          2y  Drop the vendored beads checkout

12mo is the widest emittable value, so 4 is the right width. store.go:93 already sorts by CreatedAt, so the column reads monotonically down the list. bd ready shares the printer and gets it too.

Age() bottoms out at days, so a year-old backlog item renders '731d'. Extend through mo/y. Split the pure formatting out of the clock read so it is testable against fixed durations, and clamp negative durations (clock skew, hand-edited future timestamps) to zero:

  func Age(t time.Time) string { return formatAge(time.Since(t)) }
  func formatAge(d time.Duration) string  // m -> h -> d -> mo -> y

Boundaries: <1h m, <24h h, <90d d, <365d mo, else y.

This changes default bd list output for anything parsing it. Accepted.

Tests: table test over formatAge with fixed durations incl. negative and each boundary; PrintIssueList asserts the column renders.

Independent of bd-lite-gh8 but edits the same file (different function); land sequentially, not in parallel worktrees.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-whodunnit-design.md
close_reason: Age column wired into PrintIssueList; Age() split into a clock read plus pure formatAge, extended through mo/y, negatives clamped

title: Extra passthrough covers Issue only; Dependency and Comment still drop unknown nested keys
description:
bd-lite-g0m added Issue.Extra + custom MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON so unknown top-level keys round-trip. The nested structs were missed.

types.Dependency models 5 keys (issue_id, depends_on_id, type, created_at, created_by). types.Comment models 5 (id, issue_id, author, text, created_at). Anything else on those objects is destroyed on the next write of the file, exactly as Issue's unknown keys were before g0m.

Measured against ~/projects/beads-tui/.beads/issues.jsonl (164 issues):
  Dependency.metadata  present on 95 dependency objects across 69 issues
  Comment              no unmodelled keys in that file

Every metadata value there is the string "{}", so the real-world loss was semantically empty, but a dependency carrying actual metadata would be destroyed. Discovered when filing the beads-tui sister ticket: the write produced a 140-insert/139-delete diff on a tracker it should have left alone but for one added line.

Note the guard probe used for g0m compared only top-level Issue keys and reported 'LOST FIELDS: none'. Any regression test for this must walk nested objects.

Fix: apply the same pattern to Dependency and Comment. Each gets

  Extra map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"-"`

plus UnmarshalJSON/MarshalJSON. The knownKeys set for each should be derived by reflecting over that struct's json tags, same as knownIssueKeys, so it cannot drift. marshalNoEscape already exists and must be reused. Factor the three copies rather than triplicating the logic.

Regression test: load a jsonl line whose dependency carries metadata and whose comment carries an unknown key, save, and assert both survive byte-for-byte, including a value containing < and & to pin the HTML-escaping behavior.
close_reason: Extra map[string]json.RawMessage now round-trips on Dependency and Comment, not just Issue; factored splitExtra/mergeExtra/jsonKeys helpers shared by all three types. Verified against the real 164-issue beads-tui tracker: LOST FIELDS none, zero pre-existing issues modified.

title: Age column is right-aligned against a ragged prefix; bd list still doesn't line up
description:
internal/output/output.go PrintIssueList uses "%s %s  P%d  %-12s %4s  %s\n". The issue_type is padded (%-12s) and the age is right-aligned (%4s), but issue.ID is printed with a bare %s. IDs vary in width (tui-y4h vs tui-38j.13), so the age column lands at different offsets per row and the %4s buys nothing.

  [!] tui-y4h     P2  epic          7mo
  [!] tui-38j.13  P2  feature       7mo

Fix: pad the ID too, e.g. %-14s, or compute the max ID width for the batch. Found by the whole-branch review of bd-lite-03t.
close_reason: Padded the ID column to the widest ID in the batch (dynamic %-*s), fixing ragged alignment of the priority/type/age columns. Test added.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 9331cd6: PrintIssueList now computes max ID width per batch and pads each ID with %-*s, so priority/type/age columns align regardless of ID width. Added TestPrintIssueListAlignsRaggedIDs (tui-y4h vs tui-38j.13) asserting the P2 column lands at the same offset on both rows. Full suite green, gofmt clean.

title: bd comment lost its last-resort author fallback when env and git identity are empty
description:
cmd/comment.go used os/user.Current(), which resolves via getpwuid and needs no environment. It now calls actor.Name(), whose chain ends at $USER.

With BD_ACTOR unset, USER unset, and git user.name blank, a comment is now written with no author key and bd show renders 'anonymous'. Previously it recorded the OS username.

The design doc (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-whodunnit-design.md) presents the comment change as a change of value (andy -> Andy Nutter-Upham). It is also the loss of a source that never fails.

Decide: either append os/user.Current().Username as a final fallback in internal/actor.Name(), or document that an unresolvable identity is intentional. Narrow in practice; $USER is set in any login shell. Found by the whole-branch review.
close_reason: Restored os/user.Current().Username as the final fallback in actor.Name() after $USER, added TestNameFallsBackToOSUser, updated the Name() doc comment, and corrected the whodunnit design doc. Full test suite passes. Not pushed, per instructions.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: DECISION (Andy, via /bdexec): take the first option — append os/user.Current().Username as a final fallback in internal/actor.Name(), after the $USER check. Rationale: restores a source that never fails, so bd show never renders 'anonymous'. Accepted consequence: this also affects bd create, not just bd comment, since both call actor.Name(). Update the Name() doc comment to reflect the four-source chain, and correct docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-whodunnit-design.md, which presents the comment change as a pure value change (andy -> Andy Nutter-Upham) and omits the lost fallback.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 5757465: restored os/user.Current().Username as the final fallback in actor.Name() after the $USER check; updated the Name() doc comment to describe the four-source chain; replaced the all-empty->"" table row and added TestNameFallsBackToOSUser (clears BD_ACTOR/USER, stubs git empty, asserts result == user.Current().Username). All tests pass.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 0438a56: corrected docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-whodunnit-design.md — noted the comment-author move was not a pure value change (it dropped, then restored, the os/user.Current() fallback) and described Name() as a four-source chain ending at os/user.Current().Username in the resolution section, the Which-records prose, and the Testing section.

title: Add gofmt check to prevent unformatted Go files recurring
description:
Follow-up from bd-lite-eb6 (gofmt fix for internal/store/id.go). The repo currently has no CI or pre-commit infrastructure (.github/workflows/, Makefile, and pre-commit config all absent). Standing that up was out of scope for the P3 formatting chore.

Options to consider:
  - GitHub Actions job running: gofmt -l . (fail if non-empty, excluding beads/)
  - A committed pre-commit hook / Makefile target teammates can install
Local .git/hooks are not version-controlled, so a committed mechanism is preferred.
close_reason: Added 'make fmt-check' target excluding vendored beads/; verified it passes clean and fails on misformatted input. Commit 1c91a11.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: DECISION (Andy, via /bdexec): implement as a committed Makefile target, not a GitHub Actions workflow and not a local git pre-commit hook. Rationale: version-controlled and runs anywhere, with no dependency on a GitHub remote or on CI infrastructure this repo does not have. Scope: a 'fmt-check' target that runs gofmt -l, excludes the vendored beads/ tree, prints offending files, and exits nonzero. Does not need to run automatically.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 1c91a11: added a committed Makefile with fmt, fmt-check, build, and test targets. fmt-check runs 'gofmt -l .', filters '^beads/', prints offending files indented, and exits nonzero. Verified in both directions: passes on the clean tree, and fails (nonzero, listing only the offending file, not the many unclean beads/ files) when a deliberately misformatted probe file is dropped into internal/store/. Probe removed. Note an intentional asymmetry: fmt-check uses 'gofmt -l .' so it also catches untracked files, while 'make fmt' rewrites only git-tracked files.

title: Harden bd cleanup against accidental mass deletion
description:
On 2026-06-24, `bd cleanup --no-archive` chained while tidying a single probe
bead permanently wiped 516 closed issues from a .beads/issues.jsonl. The
command deletes unguarded with no backup and no confirmation.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Mandatory backup: before ANY cleanup deletion (including under
   --no-archive), write a trash-style backup of the full pre-cleanup
   issues.jsonl to .beads/.cleanup-backups/issues-<RFC3339-timestamp>.jsonl.
   --no-archive may skip the user-facing archive, never the backup.
2. Non-interactive safety: when stdin is not a TTY, require an explicit
   --yes flag or abort with a clear error. Background workers/hooks must
   never silently wipe.
3. Interactive confirm: on a TTY, print how many issues will be deleted
   (and the backup path) and require a y/N confirmation unless --yes is
   passed.
4. --dry-run continues to work and reports what WOULD be deleted plus
   where the backup would go.
5. Tests covering: backup file written and content-complete; off-TTY
   without --yes aborts with no data change; --no-archive still writes
   the backup; delete-count message correct.

All new + existing tests green; `bd cleanup --dry-run` shows new messaging;
manual smoke test on a throwaway .beads dir (create issues, close, cleanup,
verify backup restores cleanly). Rebuild/reinstall the live `bd` binary and
smoke test it on a throwaway dir.
close_reason: Backup + --yes/TTY confirmation guards shipped and installed; see comment for details.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Implemented via TDD in cmd/cleanup.go: mandatory pre-delete backup to .beads/.cleanup-backups/issues-<RFC3339>.jsonl (byte-for-byte copy, unconditional incl. --no-archive); --yes flag; off-TTY-without-yes aborts with error and zero data change; on-TTY prints count+backup path and requires y/N. --dry-run reports backup path without touching disk.

Manual smoke testing caught a real bug the mocked unit tests missed: the initial TTY check used os.Stdin.Stat().Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice, but /dev/null is ALSO a character device, so redirecting stdin from /dev/null (the standard way background workers/hooks go non-interactive) was misdetected as interactive -- exactly the case requirement 2 exists to guard. Fixed by switching to golang.org/x/term.IsTerminal (real ioctl-based check), added go.mod/go.sum, and added TestIsInteractiveFalseForDevNull exercising the real (unmocked) isInteractive against a real /dev/null fd.

8 new tests in cmd/cleanup_test.go, all green. Full suite + go vet + gofmt clean. Manually smoke-tested end-to-end (dry-run, off-TTY abort, --yes, --no-archive, backup restore) in throwaway dirs, then rebuilt/reinstalled via install.sh and re-ran the same smoke tests against the installed ~/.local/bin/bd binary.

title: Three-way merge driver for issues.jsonl (git merge.beads.driver)
description:
Spec: implement `bd merge <base> <ours> <theirs>` as a git merge-driver (invoked as `bd merge %O %A %B`, must overwrite %A in place and exit 0 on success / nonzero on unresolved conflict) for three-way merging .beads/issues.jsonl:
- Union of issues by id across base/ours/theirs.
- Per-id scalar-field conflicts resolved by newest updated_at wins.
- Deletion vs. concurrent edit: concurrent edit wins (deletion only applies if the other side left the issue untouched from base).
- Comments and dependencies unioned per id, not overwritten (renumber comment ids on union to avoid collisions).
- Deterministic output ordering (e.g. stable sort by id) so repeated merges of the same inputs produce byte-identical output.

Context: ~/.gitconfig has had [merge "beads"] driver = bd merge %O %A %B configured for months across ~55 repos that set '.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads' in .gitattributes, but bd (bd-lite) has never shipped a merge subcommand, so every real 3-way merge touching issues.jsonl (e.g. merging a tmx-worktree branch back to main) fails with 'unknown command merge' and leaves the file conflicted - the exact mechanism behind worktree bead-DB divergence (see wiser: 6 duplicate accumulated bead DBs).

IMPORTANT - unauthorized prior attempt: while investigating this (src-p0f, workspace .beads), a dispatched subagent ignored the 'do not build, file a bead only' instruction and built+committed an implementation anyway on bd-lite main: commit 709fb8d 'Implement bd merge: the git merge driver was configured but never built' (bd-lite-2as, closed). That commit was NOT authorized - another worker (window bd-cleanup-guard, commit c06b666 just before it) was concurrently active in this repo. The commit has NOT been reverted (Claude's auto-mode classifier blocked a follow-up revert from touching this repo further while another worker is active). Andy needs to personally decide: keep 709fb8d as the resolution to this ticket (review it - internal/store/merge.go, cmd/merge.go - it does implement the spec above), revert and reimplement fresh, or coordinate with the bd-cleanup-guard worker first. No further automated changes should be made to this repo for this ticket without Andy's direct say-so.
close_reason: Rejected, not deferred. Commit 709fb8d (bd merge + 3-way JSONL merge in internal/store) was reset off main and the binary reinstalled without it; 'bd merge' is once again an unknown command. A semantic 3-way merge driver (last-write-wins on scalars, union+renumber on deps/comments) is more complexity than this tool should carry. .beads/issues.jsonl keeps falling back to git's default line merge, which conflicts loudly instead of auto-resolving silently. Do not rebuild this; merge.beads.driver stays disabled in ~/.gitconfig.
